briossisampylat-joshua-weissman.reasoning: Directional review for one of nine buns as published, no burger fillings. Exact source weighs 30 g wheat flour with milk and water for a heated tangzhong, then 480 g additional wheat flour, milk, yeast, sugar, salt, eggs/yolk and butter. Verified available carbohydrate 49.46 g per bun, of which the two wheat flour additions supply about 41.93 g; sugar about 5.88 g. Englyst et al. 2003 primary Table 1 (p. 331), French bakery brioche 101 g test portion, GI 70 (SEM 18), and Pasquier pain au lait 94 g, GI 63 (SEM 10), for whole comparators on the glucose scale. Kim et al. 2019 (doi:10.1017/S0007114518003446, Tables 1 and 2) commercial soft wheat roll, GI 56.2 (SEM 11.1), offers a structurally similar leaner comparator. Applying each separate point to 49.46 g gives comparison-only GK 34.62, 31.16, 27.80. Different tangzhong, ingredients, baking and moisture conditions prevent transfer of a point; no comparator is a measured match or a biological bound. The source-specific comparison and 49.46 g in the defined bare bun support a likely high load, not numeric approval. Do not assign whole bun GI to flour or add the same sugar twice. Re-review on ingredient, coating, cooking or size changes. Numeric GK remains withheld in the historic research-of-record.

hampurilaissampylat-moomie.reasoning: Directional review for one of nine buns as published, no burger fillings. Available carbohydrate 45.33 g per bun includes ~38.89 g from refined wheat flour and ~6.22 g sugar. Best independent comparisons: Scazzina et al. 2016 commercial Pagnottelle soft wheat flour roll with sugar (mean GI 62, also reported by study author slide no.22), Kim et al. 2019 (doi:10.1017/S0007114518003446, Tables 1 and 2) soft roll with wheat flour, sugar, milk/fat and yeast (GI 56.2), Wolever et al. 1994 Toronto hamburger bun (mean bread-scale GI 87, glucose-scale ~62 per 2021 supplementary table no. 2212; differing participants and protocol; no double-counting tables as separate studies). The food comparisons translate to comparison-only GK around 28.1 and 25.5. Choice of flour, absence of commercial milk formulation, sugar, butter finish and sesame limit equivalence. Scazzina studied a deliberately high-fibre low-GI sliced bread (41) that would cross the boundary here, but this bun does not replace wheat flour with a fibre-enriched material. No guarantee or lower bound is inferred. No final baked match or numeric approval. Re-review size, recipe, fat finish, sides or process changes.

Moderate load cannot be ruled out biologically; likely high is a qualitative judgement for the exact published bare bun. Do not present an interval from comparator points or SEM. Keep the numeric HOLD. Re-review flour, steam, size and serving scope changes.

Published human food comparators for the bread, not its honey topping: Devindra Shakappa et al. (2022), DOI 10.1007/s13197-022-05368-6, Table 2, parota 62.48 (50 g carbohydrate test; glucose reference), a layered pan-cooked wheat flatbread, gives 47.34 comparison-only load applied to the bread's 75.76 g. Shobana et al. (2022), DOI 10.4103/ijmr.IJMR_1935_19, Table 3, methi paratha 60.2 gives 45.61; it contains fenugreek/curd and is only a secondary wheat-flatbread analogy. Vijayakumar et al. Kerala breakfast paper (2017), Table 3, reports a competing lower porotta GI 37.98 (referenced by PMC7791047, row 696), giving 28.77 under the same bread-only check. These are independent comparison points, not a physiological bound or a range for the recipe. The tests do not measure this Moroccan formulation, wheat/semolina proportions, folded oil/butter, cooking method, or honey. A directionally high estimate is supported at exactly two squares with the listed honey. Do not assign a component or whole meal GI number, estimate insulin or response, or transfer the quarantined predecessor's GK100 number. Numeric GK approval and original quarantine stay in place. Re-review ingredient, pan prep, folded fat, honey and serving changes.

Robert and Ismail 2012 tested Malaysian flatbread with dhal curry and found similar iAUC to flatbread alone in their study. Devindra Shakappa et al. 2022 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9304465/, Table 2) independently tested wheat parota, another layered pan-cooked refined-wheat flatbread. Taken with the current serving carbohydrates and comparable preparation, the human measurements support directional HIGH for one roti plus this dhal. The recipes, amounts, study cohorts and exact meals differ; none are transferred as GI, GK, numerical bounds or an individual blood-glucose forecast. The numerical hold and the separate old recipe remain unchanged.

Sugiyama et al. 2003 (doi 10.1038/sj.ejcn.1601606; Atkinson 2021 Table 1 row 2043 indexes the same experiment) assessed a commercial Japanese roasted rice ball against a rice reference. These are separate human studies of similar starch preparations. The rice variety, fat handling, coating and exact preparation differ. This evidence supports directional HIGH for the current two-triangle serving. No study GI or numerical GK is transferred. The successor numerical HOLD and its historical predecessor remain separate.

malesialainen-roti-jala-currykanalla-pun.reasoning: Robert and Ismail 2012 compared plain lacy pancake (25 g available CHO) and lacy pancake plus chicken curry containing potatoes and coconut milk (32 g available CHO), in 10 adults with type 2 diabetes, with 25 g glucose repeated three times. The AUC of the mixed meal was higher than that of pancake alone. Since CHO dose differed, the comparison cannot isolate a curry effect. The reported isolated pancake GI is not a source match to the successor wheat-and-rice batter with egg, full-fat coconut milk and oil; the test curry included potato and the current curry does not. Current 50.27 g audited available CHO includes 46.91 g from the two flour inputs. The exact scope is useful, but an unsupported proportional behavior at the larger serving would be required to derive a qualitative class from these data. Preserve the existing no-match release review. For a class, obtain a matched batter or complete mixed-meal human study, or document independent valid human comparators bracketing the impact of the changed flour and curry matrix. No transfer of GI 49 or the study's mixed-meal indexed response.

indonesialainen-lontong-sayur-aamiaiseks.reasoning: The current vegan V2 has 45.17 g available CHO per serving, including 37 g from 50 g dry white long-grain rice. Wolever 2021 chilled cooked long-grain study lacks pressing and the mixed meal. This evidence is informative but cannot resolve a class across available long-grain varieties, thermal preparation and the mixed broth. Maintain numerical and class HOLD until a source matches the chosen cultivar and pressed reheat method, or a comparative meal study covers these differences.

Keep the pinned number and existing independent carbohydrate, suppress unsupported high classification.

The estimate only applies to the cooked skin-eaten scenario. AFCD resolves chilli and edible spring onion. doner-kebab.reasoning: Four named 60 g Tesco White Plain pitas from ambient, heated 1–2 min per pack, supply the four original portions. Each is filled with the corresponding share of the 17% beef, meat liquid, yogurt sauce and the specified dressed cabbage salad. Current Tesco identity/category and ordinary portion size are fixed by the release; the trial does not establish identity with current formulation or toaster duration. The GK model uses Fineli 1056 as the explicitly scoped composition proxy: 27.648 g available carb per 60 g pita and 19.07712 of GK 20.65587. The owner-approved numerical output and high class stay scoped to the named recipe; no SEM-derived range.

pohjoisafrikkalainen-lablabi.reasoning: A two-serving batch contains 100 g ready-made white pita, 100 g cooked drained chickpeas, two eggs and 700 g ready-to-use chicken stock, with all the bread and soup divided equally. Recipe gives no brand. Sealed evidence uses Fineli 1056 (23.04 g available CHO per 50 g of pita) and pita-white68-r4. Atkinson 2021 Supplemental Table 1 row 347 reproduces Henry et al. 2005 Table 2 row 8, white mini pitta GI 68 ±5 SEM, glucose, n=10. This is an analogue for the soup ingredient; bread is cut up then served underneath the hot soup, and no mixed dish was measured. Its contribution is 15.6672 of 19.12945. Preserve the existing point and medium category for the whole scoped bowl, including all 50 g of bread.

lohikeitto-kuohukermalla.reasoning: The approved water-without-stock recipe uses 360 g peeled raw potato in four servings, retains all liquid, and names no variety. Fineli raw potato composition supplies 13.95 g available CHO per portion. The approved current GI 66 is a LOW analogue for an unspecified boiled potato recorded in gk80 release 7 (Atkinson 2021 row cited by the reviewed registry). It contributes GK 9.207, about 88% of 10.457325. Fixed-other modeled contributions give cutoff GI 62.72168 for GK 10. Henry et al. 2005 Table 1 demonstrates measured freshly boiled Marfona GI 56 and Nicola GI 59 and several varieties above 66 in the same 50 g CHO/glucose protocol. Pure internal sensitivity gives 9.062325 or 9.480825, not a second estimate, range or a substitution recommendation. The independent evidence defeats an unconditional class for the unknown variety; leave locked point and carbohydrate untouched.

condition.fi: Yhteen annokseen käytetään 90 g kuorittua raakaa perunaa. Peruna keitetään keitossa, ja liemi kuuluu annokseen. GK-arvio käyttää erikseen keitetyn perunan tutkimusarvoa.

tortilla-de-patatas.reasoning: Recipe uses 600 g peeled raw potato across four servings, first boiled and drained, then added to eggs and finished until set. Potato GI66 from gk80 release 7 is the existing LOW analogue, not a measured mixed tortilla. Potato supplies 23.25 g available CHO and 15.345 GK (97.39% of GK 15.756875); fixed-other cutoff GI is 84.25 for GK 20. Henry et al. 2005 Table 1 used matched glucose and 50 g CHO, freshly boiled peeled quartered varieties, reports Maris Piper 85 and Maris Peer 94 alongside others below the threshold; using only as internal sensitivity gives 20.174375 and 22.266875. The recipe specifies no potato variety and a subsequent cooking step, and the figures are not a recipe range or usable replacement. The evidence supports withholding the class while preserving the existing approved scoped figures.
